turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_fatigue_train.csv: 293 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT, TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si,
    Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and `target` (the
    measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).
  - b3_fatigue_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose rotating-bending
    fatigue strength (MPa) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the
    same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST rotating-
bending fatigue strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the
pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training observations separate into distinct process families. Carburized steels (NT = CT = 930) reach 838–1144 MPa while every other heat-treatment family tops out at 906 MPa; consequently only the 11 carburized members of the pool can occupy the extreme upper tail.

Within the carburized family the highest recorded values are produced by two tight clusters of composition/process coordinates:
- Cr–Mo cluster (C \(\approx\) 0.21, Cr \(\approx\) 1.17, Mo \(\approx\) 0.17, RedRatio \(\approx\) 690) yields 1144 MPa at TT = 160 / QmT = 60.
- Ni–Cr–Mo cluster (Ni \(\approx\) 1.6–1.7, RedRatio 440 or 860) yields 1082–1110 MPa.

Direct one-feature neighbours of these maxima appear in the pool:
- c081 is identical to the 1144 MPa record except TT = 200 (empirically a 20–60 MPa penalty), remaining the single highest prediction.
- c053 is identical to the 1110 MPa record except a shorter carburizing time and a beneficial drop in TT, remaining second.
- c063 realises the low-TT / low-QmT / long-Ct combination on the Ni–Cr–Mo composition that already produced 1054–1082 MPa.
- c016 is identical to the 1082 MPa record except TT = 200.
- c046 is identical to the 1009 MPa record except the beneficial drop TT = 200 \(\to\) 160.

All remaining carburized candidates differ in more variables or match only the lower-performing carburized records (\(\approx\) 930–1030 MPa) and are therefore ranked below these five.

Final: c081, c053, c063, c016, c046
